clue.text: Permitted drops of water to escape, but not the ball?

definitions.text: Permitted drops of water to escape, but not the ball?

parts.words: Permitted drops of water to escape, but not the ball?
parts.note: the word for letting liquid trickle out a drop at a time is also the footballer's word for running with the ball at your feet; the question mark rules the football sense out

explanation.surface: A leaky tap lets water drip out, unlike a footballer who keeps hold of the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In football the same verb means running forward with the ball at your feet; the clue says it is the dripping sense, not the ball sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To let liquid fall in small drops or a thin trickle is exactly what this verb describes.

clue.text: Silly daughter at the back

parts.note: aft is the nautical word for at or towards the stern, the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark about a foolish daughter sitting at the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft is an informal British synonym for foolish or senseless.

clue.text: One minute before noon, prayer leader appears

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, Latin for before midday

explanation.surface: A minute before midday, the man who leads worship arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islam the imam is the person who leads congregational worship in a mosque.

clue.text: One minds young graduate being next to model

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
by means beside or next to
an artist's model is a sitter

explanation.surface: A young graduate lands a job alongside a model, as if describing someone's career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One minds young' reads like a sentence fragment, but it is the definition: someone who looks after children.
explanation.definitionFit: A person paid to look after children while parents are out is said to mind them.

clue.text: The Spanish yet to produce a cricket team?

parts.note: el is the masculine definite article in Spanish
even and yet both mean still, as in 'even more' and 'yet more'

explanation.surface: A Spanish side still hoping to put together a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a cricket side has this many players.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket side fields this number of players, so the number serves as a name for the team.

clue.text: Fashionable greeting among Conservatives

indicators.note: among tells us the greeting sits inside the pair of Conservatives

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, doubled for the plural
hi is a casual greeting

explanation.surface: A stylish hello exchanged among Tory party members.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and elegant, in keeping with current style.

clue.text: Sacred greeting by day

parts.note: hallo is a variant spelling of hello
Wed is the short form of Wednesday

explanation.surface: A holy salutation offered in the daytime.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed means made holy or greatly revered, as in hallowed ground.

clue.text: Part of goal to get from one end of pub to the other?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the horizontal bar joining the two goalposts

definitions.text: to get from one end of pub to the other?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: to traverse a bar, a pub

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words and it describes walking the length of a pub, which is why the clue ends with a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The top bar of a football or rugby goal is its standard name, and also literally crossing a bar.

clue.text: Plane maybe carrying a pair of bishops, bearing more weight?

indicators.note: the plane carries the bishops inside it

parts.note: a plane is an example of a flier, something that flies
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, so two bishops are BB

explanation.surface: An aeroplane with two bishops aboard, struggling with the extra load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing more weight' sounds like a heavier payload, but it means having more loose fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Flabbier means fatter and softer, carrying more surplus flesh.

clue.text: Muse about painting being returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: an oil is an oil painting
c is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: An artist reflects on a canvas that has been sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muse' looks like a verb meaning ponder, but it names one of the nine Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: Clio is the Greek Muse of history, one of the nine goddesses of the arts.

clue.text: Vessels: most at base, after refit

indicators.note: a refit rebuilds a ship, so the letters are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: Ships kept mostly at their home port after an overhaul.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamboats are boats driven by steam engines, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: A sister's on for making new statements

indicators.note: making something new rebuilds it, so these letters are set in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A nun or sibling is busy drafting fresh statements.
explanation.definitionFit: An assertion is a confident declaration or claim, so the plural fits statements.

clue.text: Father's dark brown — or fair?

parts.note: pa is father, plus the possessive 's
sable is a dark brown colour, from the animal's fur

explanation.surface: A question about whether Dad's complexion counts as dark or light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' looks like a light colour set against dark brown, but it means acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Passable means adequate or just good enough, which is one sense of fair.

clue.text: A little brother's sitting up in bed, rapt

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters inside the bed
in a down clue, sitting up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: bro is short for brother, plus the possessive 's

explanation.surface: A small boy sits up in bed, completely engrossed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' signals the shortened form of brother rather than a young sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rapt is wholly engrossed, which is what absorbed means.

clue.text: Top monks like to carry books and Old Testament

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside, so these letters go within

parts.note: as means like, in the way of
B is book, doubled for books

explanation.surface: Senior monks bearing books, including the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbot is the head of an abbey, the senior monk in charge.

clue.text: Film maker arrived with artist

parts.note: came means arrived
an RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A movie director turns up with a painter in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film maker' suggests a director, but it is the device that records the film.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera literally makes film footage, so it is a playful name for the device.

clue.text: One's yellow jersey, perhaps, found on a road

parts.note: a Jersey is a breed of dairy cow, so it is an example of a cow

explanation.surface: A cyclist's yellow jersey is spotted lying on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The yellow jersey suggests the Tour de France leader, but a Jersey is a cattle breed; yellow means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being yellow is slang for lacking courage, so a person who is yellow is a craven.

clue.text: Big city fails: if let off, they'll be fuming!

definitions.text: if let off, they'll be fuming!

parts.note: the Smoke is a British nickname for London, the big city
bombs means fails badly, as a show bombs

explanation.surface: A city's flops are compared to fireworks that go off in anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Smoke' is an old nickname for London; 'fuming' is both angry and giving off smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: These devices are set off to release clouds of smoke, so they literally produce fumes.

clue.text: One hundred and one becoming ninety-nine?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: An arithmetic puzzle: how can a hundred and one turn into ninety-nine?
explanation.walkthrough: A 99 is a British ice cream: a soft-serve cone with a chocolate flake pushed in.
explanation.definitionFit: The 99 ice cream is served in a wafer cone, so the cone is an example by association.

clue.text: Goes out on the beach?

parts.note: it reads like a person strolling on the sand, but it is the sea retreating from the shore

explanation.walkthrough: Someone going out on the beach is the false picture; the thing going out is the tide.
explanation.definitionFit: When the tide recedes from the shore it is said to do this, the opposite of flowing.

clue.text: Bait boss regularly, producing childish articles

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, starting with the first

parts.note: taking the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of these words

explanation.surface: Teasing the boss at work with immature behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bibs are cloths tied under a small child's chin at mealtimes, articles worn by toddlers.

clue.text: A search to the east of pet cemetery

indicators.note: in an across clue east is to the right, so the search follows the pet

parts.note: a cat is a typical pet
to comb is to search thoroughly

explanation.surface: Hunting for a lost pet somewhere east of a burial ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground burial place with tunnels and recesses for tombs.

clue.text: Finally see Hammond bowled by spinner

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of each of the following words

parts.note: the last letter of each of these four words, read in order

explanation.surface: A cricket scorecard moment: Hammond clean bowled by the spin bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: Wally Hammond was a great England batsman, and a spinner sounds like a spin bowler, but here it is swirling water.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a circular swirl of water or air, something that spins.

clue.text: Used soy sauce primarily for cooking Greek on epic journey

indicators.note: cooking means mixing up, so these letters are stirred into a new order
primarily means the first letter of sauce only

parts.note: the opening letter of sauce

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction about using soy sauce in a recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus is the Greek hero whose ten-year voyage home is told in Homer's Odyssey.
